A 48-year-old male patient comes for a follow-up visit two weeks after being discharged from a
three-week hospital stay. He had sustained femur and pelvic fractures in a head-on collision where he
was the driver. His medical history includes diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. He reports
smoking 3 packs of cigarettes daily and consuming 4 alcoholic drinks nightly. The patient reports new
difficulty engaging in sexual activity with his wife, which he states is unprecedented. He also mentions
experiencing mild headaches and insomnia, for which he takes trazodone. His vital signs show:
temperature 99.3°F (37°C), blood pressure 106/72 mmHg, pulse 86/min, respirations 10/min, and
oxygen saturation 99% on room air. What is the most probable diagnosis for his current condition?
Answer Choices: (A) Atherosclerotic change (B) Psychologic (C) Post-traumatic stress disorder (D)
Venous insufficiency (E) Hormonal imbalance (F) Autonomic dysfunction (G) Neurologic damage (H)
Vascular insufficiency (I) Medication changes (J) Chronic pain syndrome
 A. Venous insufficiency
B. Medication changes

C. Atherosclerotic change
D. Psychologic
E. Vascular insufficiency
F. Post-traumatic stress disorder
G. Neurologic damage
H. Chronic pain syndrome
I. Autonomic dysfunction
J. Hormonal imbalance
